data.summary: Process layer, milestone M1 (author vocabulary) and the first three modules of M2, against docs/PROCESS.md and docs/PROCESS_SHARDING.md. Sixteen modules under Grass/Process plus three fixture files; docs/PROCESS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md schedules the work and carries a ledger of corpus defects. lake build is green with warningAsError; no sorry, no added axioms beyond propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. The build gate and the Grass.+ glob in lakefile.toml duplicate c-mem's identical edit; lakefile.toml also gains a Tests library, and docs/README.md gains one line registering the plan. FOUR DEVIATIONS NEED RATIFICATION BEFORE THIS IS SOUND TO MERGE, all recorded in plan section 10: (10.6) InterruptReason, LogicalFault and EnvironmentViolation are carried per ProcessVocabulary rather than globally, which adds three mandatory fields to every authored ProcessSpec and therefore requires Spikes/4 and Spikes/5 plus their SPIKE_n.md blocks to change in lockstep - this branch does not change them, so the golden author surface is currently inconsistent with the library; (10.5) the terminal-remainder law is withdrawn from ProcessSpec and supplied through ProcessAcceptance, indexed by the terminal partition; (10.8) ProcessTopology carries spawn authority only, with cancellation and supervision deferred to facets; and ProcessSpec is split across two universes with ProtocolRegistry across three. THREE CORPUS DEFECTS ARE RAISED, NOT FIXED: AbstractSpecificationProcessNetwork is declared incompatibly in PROCESS.md and SEMANTICS.md; Process and Semantics are mutually dependent through DriverBoundary, which MODULES.md's strict chain does not permit; and CancellationPolicy has four incompatible arities across PROCESS.md, PROCESS_SHARDING.md and Spikes/4. KNOWN LIMITATIONS: Grass/Process/Bag.lean and the finite-set representations in Nominal.lean and Scope.lean are temporary custody pending Grass.Std.Logical and Grass.Core, handover addressee c-mem; per-process progress admits a self-delivered livelock, because nothing at this layer can declare an external event to be genuinely environmental, and excluding it is recorded as an M4 obligation; EffectDemand and EffectResult are undeclared in the corpus and Sequential/Machine.lean identifies them with the boundary's demand and result, which needs ratifying before the M4 adapter is stated over it. Four local adversarial review rounds were run by the author before nomination; they found a multiplicity-blind terminal disposition and an uninhabitable ProcessCorrect, both fixed. Those rounds were author-run agents and are not independent review.

data.observed_behavior: PROCESS.md section 2 declares ProcessEvent's interruption, fault, and violation classes unqualified, which reads as one global classification shared by every process. PROCESS_SHARDING.md section 10 lists a closed whole-program sum among its foundational failures. A global LogicalFault is that shape: HTTP/2 error codes, Vulkan device loss, zlib corruption, and a Win32 handle violation are the fault classes of unrelated subsystems, and no enumeration owned by the process layer can hold them. FOUNDATION law 8 closes the usual escape by forbidding an unclassified-other constructor. Review finding fault-vocabulary-unratified on nomination c-process:2 offers conforming to the global classification as a closure condition; taking it would implement the shape PROCESS_SHARDING section 10 names as a foundational failure, so the finding cannot be closed by conforming until this is settled.

data.expected: A DECISIONS.md entry either ratifying the split or directing c-process to restore the fields. The argument for splitting is PROCESS_SHARDING.md section 3, which requires a composition invariant to depend on the smallest facet supplying its facts, and section 10, which lists a witness indexed by the complete plan when each field consumes only a facet as a foundational failure: a ChannelContract consumes endpoints and spawn authority and not a restart-intensity window, so with all three in one record, adding a cancellation point rebuilds every channel proof.
data.observed_behavior: c-process implemented the split on nomination c-process:2. Review finding topology-laws-omitted correctly blocks on it, and raises a point the plan did not: the exported name ProcessTopology now denotes a materially weaker record than the normative structure, so a downstream consumer could hold a value of that name while assuming lifecycle authority its type does not carry. That is a naming hazard independent of whether the split is right, and c-process will address it on either outcome, by renaming the weaker record or by landing the aggregate that recovers the full normative contract.

completed: Grass/Process/Network/Assertion.lean, with fixtures. The assertion language PROCESS.md section 3's channel contracts are stated over. This is c-process's standing risk 1 and it came in at six declarations and eleven theorems, with no points-to, no magic wand, no heap and no entailment relation.

A defect in its first draft, found by adversarial review and fixed before publication, worth recording because it is exactly what standing risk 1 is about. The module claimed that framed - an assertion's proof that it reads nothing outside its footprint - was the whole content of the type. It was not. WorldAgreement supplied only a per-fragment equivalence relation, so a caller could supply equality, discharge every framed by subst at any footprint whatsoever, and reduce every framing obligation in the weave to the worlds being identical. Nothing was unsound; everything was useless, and no theorem in the module noticed. agreesGlue is the law that excludes it: any two worlds can be mixed along any set of fragments, which is the statement that the fragments are a complete independent decomposition of the world, and which the equality agreement fails.

data.observed_behavior: A faulted instance's localState says nothing about which LogicalFault it raised; a violated one's says nothing about which EnvironmentViolation occurred; cancelled determines no CancelReason and interrupted no InterruptReason. PROCESS.md section 3's own ChildLifecycleEvent carries all four, so the corpus already treats the class as part of the ending - but the instance record does not, and there is nowhere else in network state for it to go. terminated is the same defect one step milder: ProcessSpec.Terminal is a relation, so a state may be terminal with several results and a recovery from the tag returns some result rather than the one the parent's ChildDemandBinding routed. Nothing here is unsound and nothing is lost globally, since the class was delivered as an event and the parent recorded it. What is lost is that network state alone cannot answer what ended a process, so a join, a supervisor's restart-intensity accounting, or an audit reading the network has to consult the parent's transition instead of the instance.
reproduction: Read docs/PROCESS.md section 3's ChildLifecycleEvent and compare its payloads with ProcessInstance.lifecycle. Every terminal event carries its class; the field that records the same ending carries none.

Tests/Process/InstanceFixtures.lean at b56ada97398dc069a276d809d9bb6af717cc4066 builds a topology with two protocols over one vocabulary. blindSpec is terminal at zero for either answer, and blind_result_is_not_determined proves the same terminated instance is TerminatedWith true and TerminatedWith false. determinedSpec is terminal only with true, and determined_result_is_unique proves the recovered result is the recorded one there. Neither half is visible at countdown, whose TerminalResult is a singleton, so uniqueness holds there for want of a second value rather than because the protocol determines anything.

Grass/Process/Network/Instance.lean at b56ada97398dc069a276d809d9bb6af717cc4066 states TerminatedWith, which names a specific result so the obligation is at least statable, and terminated_result_unique, which states the functionality hypothesis under which the recovered and recorded results coincide. Grass/Process/Spec.lean's DeterministicProcess.terminal_functional supplies that hypothesis for the deterministic construction, and a nondeterministic protocol is legal.
